page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 extensions and AMX are not supported. The instance has no integrated local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage options, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance across multi-threaded applications. The instance achieves top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core testing (86,222.56) and PassMark CPU evaluation (61,840.51), accompanied by high-throughput Geekbench scores in software compilation (38,720.0) and ray tracing (63,759.0). Cryptographic acceleration is reinforced by top-tier PassMark CPU encryption metrics (68,414.08). In-memory database workloads demonstrate high throughput, registering 63.14 million operations per second in Redis SET operations alongside strong PassMark database scores.

Performance tradeoffs center on single-core limits and larger memory access patterns. While single-core compute performance sits in the upper and middle tiers (PassMark and Geekbench single-core at 1,571.0), uncached sequential memory bandwidth drops to average rankings (130.92 GB/sec read and 64.66 GB/sec write). Text generation for large 70B language models lands in the bottom 10% (2.41 tokens/sec), emphasizing that heavy AI inference requires specialized hardware. Lacking local disks, persistent storage throughput is dependent on attached network volumes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-64 offers high compute density and balanced memory allocation without paying for bundled GPU hardware. It is well suited for enterprise database clusters, parallel software compilation pipelines, microservice backends, CI/CD runners, and distributed batch processing environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, coupled with 256 GB of RAM at a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark profiles show strong multi-core compute capability, with top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench compilation, and PassMark encryption tests. Redis SET operations reach 63.14 million operations per second, indicating high utility for in-memory processing. However, single-core speeds and uncached memory bandwidth fall within middle percentiles, and large LLM generation performs poorly. Offering efficient compute resource density without GPU overhead, the instance is appropriate for enterprise databases, compilation pipelines, CI/CD workloads, and distributed batch operations.
